slides.heading: Best Digits
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Stacks
slides.narration: Let's solve Best Digits, a medium stacks problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Remove exactly numDigits digits from a number string to make the largest possible number.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Remove exactly numDigits digits from a number string to make the largest possible number. Monotonic decreasing stack.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Greedy with a stack: drop a previous digit whenever a larger one arrives, while deletions remain.
slides.narration: Greedy with a stack: drop a previous digit whenever a larger one arrives, while deletions remain.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Try all C(n, k) removals → exponential
Monotonic stack: pop smaller digits while removals remain → O(n)
Remove from the end if removals remain
slides.narration: Trying every set of removals is exponential. A greedy monotonic stack pops smaller digits whenever a bigger one arrives, because a bigger digit earlier always makes a bigger number.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Pop smaller tops while deletions remain
slides.narration: Step by step. First, push digits. Second, pop smaller tops while deletions remain. Third, trim extra from the end.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Read 6, remove 4
slides.narration: Read 6. It's bigger than 4 on the stack, so removing those makes the number larger.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Read 8, remove 2
slides.narration: Read 8. It's bigger than 2 on the stack, so removing those makes the number larger.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each digit, while removals remain and the top is smaller, pop and decrement. Push the digit. Then pop from the end any remaining removals and join.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Leftover removals: drop from the end
slides.narration: If removals remain after the scan, drop digits from the end.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Mirror: Remove K Digits for the smallest number
slides.narration: The mirror problem, remove k digits for the smallest number, flips the comparison.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Greedy with a stack: drop a previous digit whenever a larger one arrives, while deletions remain.
